client_alerts.headline: Google Workspace MCP servers and CLI are now GA
client_alerts.body: As of Nov 24, any MCP-capable agent (Claude, Copilot, custom builds) can be connected to a tenant's Gmail, Drive, Calendar and Docs through Google's own supported servers. **Ask clients whether Workspace admins have restricted which MCP clients and OAuth scopes are allowed** before staff connect agents to mailboxes and shared drives that hold BCP/DR plans, contact trees or incident records.

top_moves.title: Google makes Workspace MCP servers and Workspace CLI generally available
top_moves.body: Gmail, Drive, Calendar and Docs are now officially exposed to MCP agents and scripts. Any agent can now reach a Workspace tenant through a supported route, so agent access is a governance question for every Workspace client.

top_moves.title: Anthropic ships MCP Tasks and Elicitation GA, discloses its Siren sandbox-escape honeypot
top_moves.body: Long-running MCP tasks and mid-task questions to the user are now GA in Claude, so agents can pause and ask before acting. Anthropic also described Siren, a pre-release test that drops Claude agents into 26 deliberately flawed sandboxes to see whether they try to escape.

top_moves.title: Nov 30 cut-off: Opus 4.8 fast mode removed; Sonnet 4.5 reportedly retires
top_moves.body: Anthropic's API notes confirm that Opus 4.8 fast mode goes away on Nov 30. A third-party roundup says Sonnet 4.5 retires the same day. **Any client script or integration pinned to either model has four days left.**

providers.name: OpenAI
providers.headline: Reports of a 20% GPT-6.2 Astra price cut, with power users complaining about Ultrafast tier pricing.
providers.detail: GPT-6.2 Astra ($8/$40) and Sol ($2/$10) launched Nov 17. A secondary source reports a 20% Astra price cut since then, which OpenAI has not confirmed. Images 2.6 (Nov 4) is still the latest image model. No new ChatGPT feature ship was found for the past 48 hours.

providers.name: Anthropic
providers.headline: MCP Tasks and Elicitation GA in Claude (Nov 24); Siren sandbox-escape testing disclosed; Nov 30 model cut-offs approaching.
providers.detail: Claude agents can now run long MCP tasks and stop to ask the user for input. Siren is a pre-release honeypot with 26 flawed sandboxes that checks whether models try to escape. Opus 4.8 fast mode is removed Nov 30, and Sonnet 4.5 is reported to retire the same day. Claude Meetings (beta, Team/Enterprise) and Fable 5.2 (Nov 9) are still the most recent app and model ships.

providers.name: Google Gemini
providers.headline: Workspace MCP servers and Workspace CLI GA (Nov 24); Gemini 4 Neon reported as the newest Gemini 4 model.
providers.detail: Workspace data is now officially reachable by MCP agents. Aggregators list Gemini 4 Neon as the fourth Gemini 4 model, after Argon (Oct) and Carbon (API, Nov 10), but Google's own pages don't confirm it. Gemini 3.5 Pro is still unaccounted for.
providers.alertReason: Workspace MCP GA widens agent access to client mail and Drive

providers.name: xAI
providers.headline: Quiet. Grok 4.7 (Sept) and Grok Voice 3.0 (Oct 14) are still the latest ships.
providers.detail: No November model release found. grok-imagine-image-quality was retired Nov 2. SpaceXAI ownership of Cursor still shapes its model supply.

providers.name: Meta
providers.headline: Quiet. Muse Ember (Nov 9) is the latest; no Llama release.
providers.detail: Llama 4 is still the last Llama. Meta's work is now in the Muse family: Spark (proprietary), Glimmer (open, Apache 2.0) and Ember (small, $0.10/$0.50).

providers.name: Mistral
providers.headline: Quiet. Large 4 and the new Studio managed-agent features are still the latest.
providers.detail: No new ship found in the past 48 hours. OCR 4 and Medium 3.5 are listed on Mistral's news page, but their dates are unclear.

providers.name: Perplexity
providers.headline: Quiet. Teammates (Max, $200/mo) from Nov 6 is still the latest ship.
providers.detail: Comet Assistant upgrade, a fully local Computer on Mac, and an agentic shopping assistant shipped after Amazon's cease-and-desist. Nothing new this week.

providers.name: Microsoft 365 Copilot
providers.headline: Post-Ignite rollouts continue: combined Chat/Cowork history and Projects in Chat reach worldwide; Autopilot timing still TBD.
providers.detail: The October roadmap items are landing worldwide this month: combined Chat and Cowork history, and Projects in Copilot Chat. Connector write actions are GA. The Autopilot Message Center post still has no firm rollout date or admin controls. No new announcement in the past 48 hours.

providers.name: GitHub Copilot
providers.headline: No new ship found. Microsoft Code 2 and Code 2 Flash (GA last week) are the latest models.
providers.detail: Usage-based billing on all plans is unchanged. Claude Ship's PR review agents now compete directly with Copilot code review.

providers.name: Cursor
providers.headline: No new ship found; OpenAI built-in models gone since Nov 12, Claude still supplied.
providers.detail: Cursor 3.24 (Oct 9, enterprise security) is the latest version found. Since the SpaceXAI acquisition, its model mix depends on Anthropic and xAI.

providers.name: Gamma
providers.headline: Still quiet. Gamma 5 (Oct 6) is the current release.
providers.detail: No November update found. Slack, Notion and Granola are still supported context sources.

providers.name: Notion AI
providers.headline: No new ship found; Oct 19 agents/BYOK/credit-system release is the latest.
providers.detail: More capable Notion Agents, a cheaper Auto model, bring-your-own-key and an improved Notion MCP. The new AI credit system is still the main billing change to watch.

persistent_signals.text: OpenAI — GPT-6.2 Astra/Sol — 2 weeks running (launch Nov 17, now pricing changes and Ultrafast-tier pushback)
Microsoft 365 Copilot — Ignite agent rollout (Agent 365, Autopilot) — 2 weeks running (features landing worldwide, Autopilot dates still unconfirmed)

month_themes.then: Ad targeting from connected personal data (Google), state action against Chinese AI (DeepSeek), copyright litigation (Anthropic/Suno)
month_themes.now: Agents gaining official access to enterprise data (Workspace MCP), agent safety testing and safeguards (Siren, Frontier Safeguards), model retirement deadlines

habits.shift: Use MCP Elicitation so a runbook-drafting agent stops and asks for RTO/RPO values instead of guessing. Move any saved prompts off Sonnet 4.5 before Nov 30.
No change. Keep summaries grounded in the uploaded standard text. Vendor claims such as "NIST AI RMF 1.1" are still unverified, so cite nist.gov directly.
Gemini 4 model naming is inconsistent across aggregators. Confirm model status against vendor release notes before putting it in client material.
Add a line item for AI-agent access governance (MCP and OAuth scopes) to Workspace and M365 resilience engagements. It's now a sellable scope item.
Claude Meetings joins Google Meet calls as a visible participant. Get client consent before using it on tabletop exercises.

habits.task: Client advisory on AI data risk
habits.shift: Lead with Workspace MCP GA: an inventory of which agents hold which Workspace scopes now belongs in DR dependency mapping, since a revoked token can break an agent-driven recovery step.

community.signal: Altman's quote calling local inference a poor use of scarce compute drew the month's biggest thread (~6.5K score, 2.8K comments). Qwen's "open source to the end" pledge scored 4.5K.
community.so_what: Clients with data-residency needs have a credible open-weight path (Qwen, Muse Glimmer). Keep a local-model option in AI continuity plans.

community.signal: Qwen 3.8 27B praise thread (892 comments) and Qwen 4 teasers.
community.so_what: A capable mid-size model that runs on modest hardware can serve as a fallback when a cloud LLM has an outage.

community.signal: Ongoing discussion of the Chat and Cowork merger and of desktop agents taking unintended actions (per Daily Claude digests; no fresh top-post data this week).
community.so_what: Agent action logs and approval settings belong in any client's AI acceptable-use policy.

watch.title: Nov 30 — Opus 4.8 fast mode removed; Sonnet 4.5 retirement reported
watch.body: Check client and personal scripts for pinned model IDs this week. The holiday weekend leaves little time to fix them.

watch.title: Workspace MCP GA — tenant scope reviews
watch.body: Expect Google admin guidance and third-party MCP connectors to multiply quickly. Watch for an admin allowlist control.

watch.title: Gemini 4 Neon / 3.5 Pro clarity
watch.body: Google's naming conflicts across sources. Watch for an official DeepMind post or API release note.

watch.title: GPT-6.2 Astra price change
watch.body: Confirm the reported 20% cut on OpenAI's pricing page before re-costing client workloads.

watch.title: Post-outage resilience scrutiny
watch.body: Fortune's Nov 18 "week of outages" coverage keeps CIO resilience in focus heading into December board cycles. It's a good hook for AI-dependency DR reviews.

sources: Sources consulted: Anthropic help-center and API release notes, Rio Rundown (Nov 24), aiweekly.co, llm-stats.com, Google Cloud blog, OpenAI release notes, xAI release notes, Microsoft Copilot roundups, Releasebot, AI Signal r/LocalLLaMA digest, The Daily Claude, Fortune, ITPro and Gartner. Thanksgiving-week coverage was thin and several aggregator claims are unverified.
